chunks: So let the worker among you work during his days of respite, before the exhaustion of his term, and in his leisure before the time of his busyness, and in his breathing space before he is seized by suffocation, and let him prepare for himself and his journey, and let him take provision from his place of departure for his place of stay.

key_terms.إِرْهَاقِ أَجَلِهِ: the exhaustion/arrival of his appointed term
key_terms.مَهَلِهِ: his respite or period of grace

ai.seo_question: How should one prepare for death according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali employs the metaphor of a traveler preparing for a permanent journey to urge believers to act while in a state of ease and capacity, before the onset of death's distress. This exhortation highlights the Shia emphasis on proactive spiritual preparation (tadbir) during the 'period of respite' (mahalah), ensuring one's deeds are sufficient for the transition from the transient world to the eternal abode.
